name: Hananiah
overview: Hananiah was a male figure known as the false prophet and identified as the son of Azzur. His role as a false prophet marks him as a significant, though negative, character within the biblical narrative. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hananiah means 'YHWH is gracious,' reflecting a common theophoric element in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's grace. This proper name, however, was not given by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Hananiah is explicitly identified as the son of Azzur. It is inferred that he had a relationship with Zedekiah, possibly as a father figure, although this is not explicitly stated. Beyond these connections, Scripture does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Hananiah's significance lies primarily in his role as a false prophet during a critical period in Israel's history. His opposition to true prophecy, particularly in contrast to the messages delivered by Jeremiah, highlights the spiritual conflict present at that time. His actions and words serve as a cautionary example of misleading prophecy against God's revealed truth.
